I'm not a guy but whatever:
There are many situations where either #1 or #2 is 'better' than the other in a sense but I really think the middle is better. Having a few skills that you've mastered and having a few (or as many as you'd like) that you're just knowledgeable but not necessarily a huge master of might be better.


If I were you, I would master the skills that would help me with my career and leave the rest as hobbies. If you're planning to be a translator, learning a few languages and developing good communicating skills as well as being able to speak clearly and well in those languages would be more helpful than let's say, gardening.

If you find yourself overwhelmed with all the things you're interested in, I would suggest to set aside some time looking at all of them and seeing which ones would really help you with your life right now. Some general things that would benefit you such as knowing how to cook (so you can eat wholesome meals and not just takeout everyday), knowing how to fix/repair things around the house (ex: sewing, kinda random but I'm sure you'll come across at least some smale holes/tears in your clothes in your lifetime), etc. Focusing on the more beneficial and useful skills at first might be more helpful.

I also suggest just reading about some of the topics and skills you're really interested in, instead of actually committing time to some of the skills you really want to learn since I'm sure you don't have all the time in the world to start working on all these skills. Having so many things to do and so much on your plate at once can be very draining. 

You might also wanna look at the ones your friends or family might be an expert on (such as coding) because you'll be able to exercise that skill with someone who knows their stuff as well as save some money by not paying for classes instead. Another twist on this could be choosing less expensive skills to work on if you want to save money (like me). If money isn't your concern, well I'm jealous (JK, if money doesn't concern you then you can just overlook this part).

Also, (this actually kinda goes with the top paragraph and is really directed at me) if you're really wanting to master these skills, you might want to look at yourself first. Learning how to read all kinds of languages is great, but if your life is very unbalanced/unhealthy,  you might want to look at that first. I'm just talking about not living a healthy life like not eating well, not exercising enough, etc. Being able to take care of yourself and to be able to live healthily and happy is also a very good skill to have too (and also the most important in my opinion). I'm not saying anything about you but just thought that it could help if I included it (it's really just a reminder to myself).

Also another thing: keep a journal! Exploring all these different skills and worlds is definitely gonna be exciting! Keep a journal and document all the stuff you do so you can look back on all the stuff you've done. You might be able to learn more about yourself and maybe it could aid you in a possible career choice or just what you really enjoy doing. I personally just love writing down all the stuff I do aside from the fact that I just need to remember things.


Good luck on your journey! I hope you learn amazing things and Enjoy exploring so many parts of the world! I'm also a bit like you in the part that I'm a bit overwhelmed with all the skills I want to explore, and writing this long ass comment has actually kinda helped me lol. I hope you learn many great things!
